finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::createclient disables tls certificate verification (`rejectunauthorized: false`) whenever sslenabled is set, so "ssl" connections are mitm-able
evidence: The supplied copy of packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts confirms `createClient` builds the pg Client with `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false` immediately above the newly added `types: { getTypeParser: datasourceTypeParser }` line, and `password: decrypt(ds.password)` is sent on that connection. With `rejectUnauthorized: false` the driver encrypts but does not authenticate the server certificate, so an active MITM presenting any self-signed cert can capture the decrypted datasource credentials and query traffic; no CA/`sslmode`/verify option is plumbed through the DTOs (datasource.dto.ts only has `sslEnabled: boolean`) or the Prisma model, so the claim's "no verify option anywhere" is also accurate. The one caveat is scope: this line is pre-existing and untouched by the diff — the PR only adds the `types` option to the same object literal — so it is a valid observation about the code as written but not a regression introduced here.
